1  Roles, and what each one can do

Every account has exactly one role. The role decides which pages the person can open and which records they can see. Choose it when you create the account — it can be changed later.

RoleIntended forCan see
AdminGreenCircle staff who manage the systemEverything, including Administration and User Management
AnalystGreenCircle staff who work on certificatesAll certificates and internal views; no Administration
ExternalA certified company's own staffOnly their own company's certificates. No Add or Edit certificate buttons, no internal tags
PartnerA partner organisation such as Amazon or NoviOnly certificates associated with that partner
PublicRarely used — the public directory needs no accountThe public certificate directory only
The two “company” fields are not the same thing

User Company is free text describing who the person works for — a label. Company Access is the list of companies whose data they are allowed to see — a permission. Filling in the first does not grant any access.

2  Creating a user account

Only Administrators can create accounts.

  1. Sign in, then open Administration → User Management.
  2. Click Add New User, at the top right of the list.

Complete the form. Fields marked with a red asterisk are required.

FieldRequired?Notes
NameRequiredThe person's full name, as it should appear in the user list
EmailRequiredMust be unique — no two accounts may share an address. Password-reset links and verification codes go here, so it must be a mailbox the person can open
RoleRequiredSee section 1. Choosing External or Partner reveals extra fields — see section 3
StatusRequiredActive lets the person sign in; Inactive blocks them without deleting the account
User CompanyOptionalFree text — their employer. A label only; it grants nothing
PasswordRequiredMinimum 8 characters
Require password reset on next loginOptionalRecommended. The person chooses their own password the first time they sign in, so the one you typed is never their long-term password
  1. Click Save User.
  2. Tell the person their username and temporary password. The system does not email new accounts — creating an account sends nothing, so you must pass the details on yourself, through a channel other than email where possible.
If the email address is already in use

Saving is refused and a message names the address. Each address may belong to only one account. Either use a different address, or change the other account first to free it up.

3  Giving access to companies or partners

External and Partner accounts see nothing until they are scoped. The relevant fields appear after you choose the role — so set the role first.

External — choose the companies

A Company Access list appears. Tick every company whose certificates this person may see. Most external users need exactly one.

Partner — choose the partner

A Partner dropdown appears. Select the one organisation this account represents.

Check this before you finish

An External or Partner account with nothing selected can sign in and will see an empty list. That looks like a broken system to the person using it, and it is the most common mistake when setting these accounts up. Always confirm the scope is set before you hand over the credentials.

4  Managing an existing user

Each row in User Management has an Actions menu at the far right.

OptionWhat it does
Edit UserChange name, email, role, status, company or partner access. You may also set a new password here — leave the password box blank to keep the current one
View 2FA StatusShows whether two-factor authentication is on, and by which method
Enable 2FATurns two-factor authentication on. See the note below
Disable 2FATurns it off and removes any authenticator enrolment
Reset 2FAClears the existing authenticator enrolment so the person can set up a new device — use this when someone loses their phone
Delete UserRemoves the account. Some accounts are protected and cannot be deleted
What “Enable 2FA” actually does

It switches two-factor authentication on and marks the account as intending to use an authenticator app — but it cannot set up the app for them. Until the person enrols their own device, codes are emailed to them instead, and the next time they sign in they are shown the setup page automatically. Nobody is locked out in the meantime.

5  Signing in

  1. Enter your username or email address — either works.
  2. Enter your password.
  3. Select Sign In.
  4. If two-factor authentication is on for your account, you are asked for a 6-digit code next.

6  Two-factor authentication

Two-factor authentication asks for a short code in addition to your password, so knowing the password alone is not enough to reach your account. Two methods are available.

MethodHow the code reaches youNotes
EmailSent to your registered address each time you sign inNothing to install. Codes expire after 5 minutes
Authenticator appGenerated on your phone, no email neededMore secure and works without a signal. Recommended

Text-message (SMS) codes are not available.

Read the instruction on the page

It names the method your account is actually using. If it says the code was emailed, a code from an authenticator app will not work — and vice versa.

If you have more than one code in your inbox

Only the most recent code works. Requesting or triggering another one cancels the previous. If in doubt, choose Resend code and use the newest email.

Your own settings live under Two-Factor Preferences, where you can see the current method and start authenticator setup.

7  Setting up an authenticator app

If your administrator has turned on two-factor authentication for you, this page appears automatically the next time you sign in. You can also reach it from Two-Factor Preferences at any time.

  1. Install an authenticator app on your phone if you do not have one — Microsoft Authenticator and Google Authenticator both work.
  2. Remove any earlier “GCC Database” entry from the app first. An old entry from a previous attempt will keep producing codes, and none of them will be accepted.
  3. In the app, add an account and choose to scan a QR code.
  4. Scan the code on screen. If the camera will not cooperate, use the Manual Entry Code shown beneath it.
  5. Type the 6-digit code the app displays into 6-Digit Verification Code, then select Enable Authenticator.
  6. Save your recovery codes. They are shown once and never again.
Recovery codes are your only way back in

If you lose the phone and have no recovery codes, an administrator must clear your enrolment with Reset 2FA before you can sign in again. Store them somewhere other than the phone itself.

From the next sign-in onward the code comes from the app and no email is sent. If an email still arrives, the setup did not complete — return to this page and finish it.

8  Resetting a password

If you have forgotten your password

  1. On the sign-in page, select Forgot your password?
  2. Enter your email address and submit.
  3. Open the email titled Password Reset - GCC Database and select the link inside. It expires after one hour.
  4. Choose a new password and confirm it.
  5. Sign in with the new password.
The confirmation message is deliberately vague

The page shows the same wording whether or not the address belongs to an account. That is intentional — it stops the form being used to discover which addresses are registered. It also means the confirmation is not proof that an email is on its way. If nothing arrives within a few minutes, check your spam folder first, then confirm the address is the one on your account.

If an administrator is resetting it for you

An Administrator can set a password directly through Edit User, without email. They should tick “Require password reset on next login” so you choose your own password immediately afterwards.

9  Troubleshooting

What you seeWhat it usually means
“Invalid email or password” — and you are sure the password is rightMost often the account is temporarily locked. Five failed attempts lock it for 15 minutes, and the message is the same as for a wrong password. Wait 15 minutes and try once — repeated attempts during the lock achieve nothing. Also check you are using your username or full email address, not a shortened version of either
“Invalid or expired code”Either the code is older than its 5-minute life, a newer code has replaced it, or it came from the wrong place — an authenticator code when the page asked for an emailed one. Re-read the instruction on the page, then use Resend code
The setup page rejects your authenticator codeUsually an old “GCC Database” entry still in the app. Delete every GCC entry, reload the setup page, and scan the fresh QR code
No email arrivesCheck spam first. If it is genuinely missing, contact your administrator — the address on the account may not be the one you are watching
An external user signs in but sees no certificatesTheir Company Access is almost certainly empty. An administrator can add it through Edit User
Lost the phone with the authenticatorUse a recovery code if you saved one. Otherwise an administrator must use Reset 2FA, after which you can enrol a new device
Access Denied after signing in successfullyThe account signed in, but the page belongs to a role it does not have. This is not a sign-in fault — check the account's role with an administrator

10  Importing users in bulk

User Management can create many accounts at once from a CSV, which is worth using from about a dozen people upwards.

  1. Click Download Template to get the empty file.
  2. Fill in the columns: Name, Email, Role, Status, User Company.
  3. Click Import and choose your file.
  4. Read the result. Rows that could not be created are listed with the reason.

User Company accepts several company names separated by semicolons, or the single word `All`.

Imported accounts have no password you can pass on

There is deliberately no password column — a spreadsheet is not a safe place for one. Each imported account gets a long random password that is never displayed, and is marked as needing a reset. The only way in is the Forgot password link, so every imported person must be able to receive email at the address you entered.

If someone must be given access immediately and cannot wait for email, create that one account with Add New User instead and hand them the password directly.

Giving an existing user a known password

Open the account in Edit User, type a new password, and save. Leaving the password field blank keeps the current one. Tick Require password reset on next login so they replace it straight away.

Glossary

TermMeaning
AdminInternal role with full access, including the Administration menu. Administrator accounts cannot be deleted
AnalystInternal role that operates the certificate work day to day — create, edit, import, export. No Administration menu
ASINAmazon Standard Identification Number, the identifier Amazon uses for a product
BadgeableA certificate that is commercially in force: Client Approved - Paid, Client Approved - Confidential, or Republished, inside its certification period
Certification #The number identifying a certificate. Assigned by the system when the certificate is saved, never typed
Certification periodThe span from the effective date to the expiration date, inclusive of both
Certification ResultsFree text recorded against a certificate, shown exactly as it was entered. Required for Amazon CPF certificates
Client Approved - ConfidentialIn force and badgeable, but deliberately withheld from the public database. An embargo, not a pause
Client Approved - PaidIn force and listed publicly
Company userA person from a certified company, signing in to see their own company's certificates. The role is named External
CPFAmazon's Climate Pledge Friendly programme
Database Listing URLThe public address of a single certificate, for sharing with someone who has no account
Effective dateThe first day a certificate is in force. It is live on this date
Expiration dateThe last day a certificate is in force. It is live through this date and expires the day after
External tagA tag visible to company and partner accounts and on public surfaces
GTIN · EAN · UPCProduct identifiers recorded against a certificate alongside ASIN
Internal tagA tag visible only to GreenCircle staff. Never shown to a company or partner account
PartnerA role for a partner organisation, scoped to the certificates associated with that partner
PathwayAn optional certification pathway on a certificate, used for Amazon CPF
Product category · type · subcategoryThe three levels of the product hierarchy. The category must exist before a product can use it
PublicThe anonymous public directory. No account is needed
RepublishedA certificate re-issued with a fresh certification period. In force and listed publicly

Getting help

Before contacting anyone, three things resolve most problems on their own.

  1. Check this guide's contents. The answer is often in another section — the troubleshooting table in particular lists the symptoms that have actually been reported.
  2. Sign out and sign back in. This clears anything left over from an interrupted session.
  3. Reload the page. If the site has been updated recently, a reload picks up the new version.

If the problem persists, report it with these five details. They are what makes a problem reproducible rather than a description of a feeling.

IncludeExample
What you were trying to do"Upload a certificate for a new product"
What happened insteadThe exact wording of any message on screen
The certificate numberIf the problem concerns a particular certificate
Browser and device"Chrome on Windows 11", "Safari on an iPad"
Roughly whenThe date and approximate time, so the event can be found

A screenshot of the whole browser window, including the address bar, is worth all five.
